correctness.rationale: Under exact canonical Loday infix coordinates a local right rotation changes exactly two coordinates by +/-ac, reproducing the known sqrt(2) ac metric. A unique binary context and three subtrees give M_N(a,c)=C_{a-1}C_{c-1}[z^(N-a-c)]T(z)/(1-2T(z)) and exact central-binomial coefficients. The differentiated Catalan series produces total length W_N. Central-binomial asymptotics prove the uniform-edge product limit; unit total limit mass gives tightness. Stirling bulk estimates, normalization W_N~4^N sqrt(N)/(16 sqrt(pi)), and explicit O(sqrt(epsilon)) control of all three boundary strips prove the Dirichlet weak limit. The standalone exhaustive integer checker independently confirms each rotation, coordinate difference, outer-size multiplicity, count, sum and maximum for N=3..8; finite checks are not used as infinite proofs.

originality.rationale: Loday (arXiv:math/0212126, Sec. 2.10) explicitly gives the local metric length sqrt(2)·ac and the maximum edge length; both are treated as prior work. A000531 independently lists the integer sequence that equals total normalized edge length, so its numerical sequence and binomial evaluation are also not asserted as new. The inspected sources and available public mathematical claim searches did not state or directly imply the full two-parameter Catalan-binomial spectrum together with the discrete independent Catalan fringe limit and the macroscopic Dirichlet(1/2,1/2,1/2) length-biased law. Exact marked-rotation enumeration and boundary-controlled asymptotic analysis supply genuinely additional mathematical statements. Historical priority remains best-knowledge, not certified.
residual_risks: Pre-existing Loday Sec.2.10 local edge-length formula and maximum are explicitly not new.
The scalar total-length integer sequence is OEIS A000531; novelty is not based on its isolated numerical values.
An unindexed marked-tree-rotation distribution or a published Catalan forest sampling theorem could imply one of the probability limits; not all global literature can be exhaustively searched.
Some related indexed public results were compared only through statements/abstracts, not their complete bodies.

value.rationale: The exact two-parameter Euclidean edge spectrum is a natural global metric invariant of the canonical associahedron, not an arbitrary slice or only a recomputation of a known number sequence. It exposes a mathematically substantive conflict between two canonical edge samplings: uniform edges have tight, heavy-tailed lengths with a diverging linear mean, whereas Euclidean-length sampling produces macroscopic Dirichlet(1/2,1/2,1/2) leaf proportions. This connects geometric one-skeleton measure, Catalan fringe decomposition and Dirichlet boundary concentration; the exact count and limiting law can inform geometric metric questions for other realizations. Claimed value rests on the distributional and structural law, not on Loday's prior local formula or known A000531 values.
